studies.title: The Structure and Dynamics of the Online MAHA-sphere
studies.volume: 234M submissions and 1.3B comments screened; 45,599 users active every year analysed; 36,803 unique MAHA-stance users
studies.method: Keyword search → Sentence-BERT relevance classifier → few-shot LLM stance labelling (pro / anti / neutral) across 12 themes; user stance score from −1 to +1
findings: 70% of MAHA-stance users were captured by r/politics alone; 82% by r/politics + r/AskReddit; 95% by the top 30 subreddits — the discourse lives in mainstream political spaces, not niche communities.

MAHA stances on Vaccine, Mask, Fluoride, Climate and Science co-occur 2–2.5× more than chance; mainstream themes (Food, Exercise, Screen, Environment) barely predict each other. Anti-MAHA users show no comparable bundling.
Pharma, Vaccine and Science form the network hub; Food and Exercise sit at the periphery — the opposite of the movement's public food-first framing.
Vaccine skepticism acts as an entry point: 6.8% (2021–22) and 11.1% (2023–24) of vaccine-theme users migrated to broader anti-science discourse the following year.
MAHA-stance users scored lower on cognitive-processing language in 8 of 12 themes and higher on money-related language in Vaccine, GMO, Pharma and Science.

studies.title: Hiding in Plain Sight: Finding MAHA on Reddit
studies.method: Two-stage regex search over ~20B posts; relevance classifier F1 0.978; LLM stance labels (4-class F1 0.56 on a 325-item hand-coded test set)
findings: Roughly 30% of active users held MAHA stances on the most contested themes (Science, Fluoride, EMF, Pharma).
MAHA-distinctive vocabulary: 'monsanto, bayer, big ag' (GMO); 'propaganda, censorship, media' (Science). Anti-MAHA: 'misinformation, evidence, spreading'.
Stance labelling is noisy (F1 0.52–0.56 vs 0.25–0.33 chance), so platform-wide pro/anti shares are not reported by the authors.

studies.title: #MakeBeefGreatAgain: A Cross-Platform Analysis of Early #MAHA Discourse
studies.platform: TikTok, X, Facebook, Instagram, Reddit, YouTube, web articles (NewsWhip Spike, high-engagement sample)
studies.method: Structural topic modelling; interrupted time series around Election Day; LLM-assisted agenda coding
findings: 39.0% of posts were 'patriotic partisan support' using #MAHA as a slogan; 23.2% electoral campaign; 21.6% healthy lifestyle; 16.2% health policy.
81.3% of posts did not engage with any of the campaign's five stated priorities; of those that did, 61.5% concerned chronic disease and 0.1% habitat preservation.
Election Day produced a +647 posts/day spike, followed by a significant decline of −21.7 posts/day — attention was event-driven, mirroring the Google Trends pattern.
TikTok functioned as the grassroots partisan-support space; X, Facebook, YouTube and web articles leaned policy/campaign; Instagram and Reddit leaned healthy-lifestyle.
